newsitem.title: CHINA: HK banking shares slide on interbank rate hike.
newsitem.headline: HK banking shares slide on interbank rate hike.

text.p: Shares of Hong Kong banks fell sharply on Tuesday as a surge in interbank rates, amid fears of a speculative attack on the Hong Kong dollar, fuelled concerns that banks' funding costs would rise and squeeze profit margins.
"The short-term outlook for local banks is pessimistic and I recommend a short-term sell on the sector," said Alex Wong, banking analyst at Dharmala Securities.
The Hang Seng finance sub-index slid 616 points, or 3.04 percent, to 19,621, while the blue chip Hang Seng Index was off 463 points, or 2.88 percent, at 15,633 in late morning trade.
The overnight rate was at 9.50-10.00 percent at late morning after briefly touching a high of 18.00-20.00 percent early this morning.
The Hong Kong dollar weakened to HK$7.7427/37 from the local opening of HK$7.7400 but was off Friday's low of HK$7.7500.
"Mortgage rates will be the first thing that banks will consider raising and that could further affect their mortgage business growth in the longer term," Wong said.
HSBC, which went ex-dividend, fell HK$7.53 to HK$262.00, while Hang Seng Bank dived HK$3.00 to HK$101.50. Bank of East Asia lost HK$0.70 to HK$30.60.

But Alan Hutcheson, banking analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said he did not expect local banks to be affected a great deal since they tended to be net lenders to the interbank market and would benefit from the higher rates.
But he said he was generally pessimistic on the banking sector and recommended a "hold" on HSBC shares and "sell" on Hang Seng Bank and Bank of East Asia.

"Basically they are seeing quite a heavy decline in net interest margins especially in the second half of the year," he said. "Rising interest rates certainly won't help their funding cost," he added.
